title: Concurrent NAO gave no clear added winter sea-level reconstruction gain at five Mid-Atlantic gauges in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether the concurrent monthly North Atlantic Oscillation index adds winter sea-level information after local memory, target month and trend control. Separate gauge fits used only earlier years. The five fixed NOAA Mid-Atlantic records gave 67 accepted January-March months in 2000-2025. Added NAO reduced pooled mean squared reconstruction error by 8.04%. Root mean squared error fell from 73.20 to 70.20 mm. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -7.56% to +21.03%. One- and five-year blocks also left the sign uncertain. Local-memory, trend and training-window checks did not resolve a gain. This is a null added-information benchmark, not a forecast or causal effect estimate. The same-month index, revised inputs, selected sites, missing months, fixed linear response and short dependent test limit inference. The package includes numerical public-domain inputs, source URLs and hashes, new code, all held-out results, bootstrap evidence, an arithmetic audit and a static figure.

display.caption: Adding concurrent NAO gave uncertain winter reconstruction gains. Error intervals use paired three-year calendar blocks. Positive values mean lower error. The early-start check first has an eligible target in March 1999. No accepted primary target exists in 2002 or 2003; absent bars are gaps.
